clue.text: Clothes in a cupboard

definitions.meaning: a person's whole stock of garments, as in a film's costume department
a tall closet with a rail for hanging garments

explanation.surface: Someone notes where the garments are kept: hung in the closet.
explanation.definitionFit: The same word names both a collection of garments and the tall piece of furniture they hang in.

clue.text: Merseyside town widens out

indicators.note: out signals the letters are put out of their usual order

explanation.surface: A northern English town is spreading wider.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges WIDENS. Merseyside is the area of north-west England around Liverpool.
explanation.definitionFit: An industrial town on the Mersey estuary, by Runcorn, in the Liverpool area.

clue.text: Rugby's station to be reddish-brown

parts.note: RU is rugby union, plus the possessive S
to station something is to set or place it

explanation.surface: The station at Rugby, an English town, is to be painted an autumnal colour.
explanation.walkthrough: Rugby is also an English town with a well-known railway junction, which sells the surface. 'to be' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A colour name for the brown-red of autumn leaves and of a type of apple.

clue.text: Charge again in the gallery?

parts.note: suggests an art gallery reselling at a fresh price, but in a shooting gallery a charge is the gun's ammunition, put in again

explanation.surface: An art gallery bills its visitors a second time.
explanation.definitionFit: To put fresh ammunition into a gun, as a marksman at a shooting gallery does between rounds.

clue.text: Bert upset about being in, it sounds

indicators.note: about means around, so the shuffled name surrounds the next piece
upset means knocked over or disordered, so the name's letters are rearranged

parts.note: being in means being at home

explanation.surface: Bert is upset about staying indoors, apparently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns BERT into B...TER, and 'about' wraps that around AT HOME. The definition plays on 'sounds' as measuring water depth.
explanation.definitionFit: An instrument for measuring the depth of water, and to sound is to measure depth.

clue.text: Moneypenny perhaps-a distinguishing title

indicators.note: perhaps suggests something tentative or variable, telling us the letters can be rearranged

parts.note: split as MONEY plus penny, abbreviated to P as in old British coinage

explanation.surface: A remark that Miss Moneypenny, Bond's secretary, is a fine example of a character name that has become a byword.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the single word as MONEY + PENNY, with penny shortened to P (the British abbreviation, as in 50p). 'perhaps' then rearranges MONEYP.
explanation.definitionFit: A name or title derived from a person, which marks out a thing or place by naming it after them.

clue.text: Gets going with the profit

definitions.meaning: the money taken from a sale or event

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means advances onward; as a plural noun it means the takings from a sale.

clue.text: Bird gets a nasty shock after dark

indicators.note: the shock comes after the darkness, so it goes second

parts.note: dark as a noun is nighttime
a jar is a jolt or unpleasant shock

explanation.surface: A bird is given a fright once darkness falls.
explanation.definitionFit: A nocturnal bird with a churring call, also called a goatsucker.

clue.text: May can be short for this lady

definitions.text: May can be short for this lady

parts.words: May can be short for this lady
parts.note: May looks like the verb or a month, but it is a pet form of a woman's full first name

explanation.surface: A remark that someone may well be brusque with a certain woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's name whose diminutives include May, Maggie, Peggy and Meg.

clue.text: Dismal waste!

definitions.meaning: as a verb, to lay waste to or devastate a place

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both an adjective for a bleak, forlorn scene and a verb meaning to ravage a land.

clue.text: Smithy right for a counterfeiter

parts.note: a blacksmith's workshop, also called a forge

explanation.surface: A blacksmith's workshop is said to be just the place for a faker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is only a link here, joining wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who fakes documents or banknotes is a counterfeiter, from the sense of forging metal into shape.

clue.text: Lift a muscle

definitions.meaning: a cage that carries people between floors
a muscle whose job is to raise a body part

explanation.definitionFit: American usage calls a passenger lift by this name, and anatomy uses it for any muscle that raises a part.

clue.text: Girl with a bed on board first

indicators.note: the bed on board comes first, ahead of the letter A

parts.note: a sleeping place on a ship or train is a berth

explanation.surface: A young woman sails with a cabin bed booked ahead of everyone else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is a link; 'first' tells you the berth goes before A.
explanation.definitionFit: A traditional female first name, so a girl.

clue.text: Europe, for example, to admit key mission

indicators.note: to admit means to let in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: Europe is an example of a continent
G is a musical key

explanation.surface: A plan to let a key diplomatic delegation into Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: A group sent to represent others, like a delegation or mission.

clue.text: Doesn't care about being poor

indicators.note: about here means turned around or scattered, telling us to rearrange the letters

explanation.surface: Someone indifferent to the quality of their work ends up with a shoddy result.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges the ten letters of DOESNT CARE (the apostrophe is ignored); 'being' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Something of inferior quality is called poor, below the first rank.

clue.text: Pa back with Ma, say? That is understandable

indicators.note: back means the short word is read in reverse

parts.note: Ma is an example of a parent

explanation.surface: Dad returns alongside Mum, which makes sense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns PA into AP; 'with' and 'That is' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain to see and so easy to grasp, as with an obvious or evident point.

clue.text: Writer about to concur to a beautiful shade of craft for elopers

definitions.text: a beautiful shade of craft for elopers

indicators.note: about means around, so the writer goes around the next piece

parts.note: a pen is a writing instrument
to concur is to agree

explanation.surface: An author agrees to describe the lovely colour of a runaway couple's boat.
explanation.walkthrough: In Edward Lear's poem The Owl and the Pussy-cat, the two lovers elope to sea 'in a beautiful pea-green boat'.
explanation.definitionFit: Lear's eloping owl and cat sailed in a boat of this light yellowish-green colour.

clue.text: One is out out in bad weather

definitions.text: One is out out in bad weather

parts.words: One is out out in bad weather
parts.note: the doubled out reads like a typo, but the craft is out at sea in storms, out on rescue

explanation.surface: Someone is caught outdoors in a storm.
explanation.definitionFit: A rescue vessel launched to save people at sea, typically when storms strike.

clue.text: Chief executives make quiet lodgers

parts.note: P is piano, the musical direction for softly
people living in a house or hotel are its residents

explanation.surface: Heads of state supposedly make for very considerate house guests.
explanation.walkthrough: 'make' is a link. P comes from piano, the musical instruction meaning soft.
explanation.definitionFit: Heads of a republic, or of a company in American usage, are chief executives.

clue.text: Kick up a row in form?

definitions.meaning: British informal: make a fuss or complain loudly
to bring into being or make

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to bring into being, and in British slang to make a fuss.

clue.text: Plant producing car in a new design

indicators.note: a new design means the letters are arranged in a new way

explanation.surface: A factory is building a car to a fresh blueprint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new design' rearranges CAR IN A; 'producing' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A mountain flower whose extract is used to soothe bruises.

clue.text: Stick notice in this very spot

parts.note: an advertisement is a notice, shortened to ad
here means in this place

explanation.surface: Fix the notice right in this place.
explanation.definitionFit: To stick fast to a surface or cling to something.

clue.text: Early invaders were crooks

definitions.meaning: a Germanic tribe that settled in England in the 5th century, giving the country its name
bends or corners, as where lines meet

explanation.definitionFit: The tribe who gave England its name share their spelling with bends or corners, so both senses fit.

clue.text: Find out about uncommon photography at night

indicators.note: about means around, so the shuffled letters go around the next piece
out suggests something put out of order, so the letters of find are rearranged

parts.note: uncommon means rare

explanation.surface: Someone discovers a little-known kind of photography that works in darkness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' turns FIND into INFD, and 'about' wraps INF...D around RARE.
explanation.definitionFit: Film or sensors working beyond the red end of the spectrum can take pictures in darkness, the classic night photography.

clue.text: Team makes one change-the flight controller!

indicators.note: the team word is altered by changing a single letter of it

parts.note: a football or cricket side has eleven players, so a team is an eleven

explanation.surface: A coach alters the line-up by one player, shouting about the man in air-traffic control.
explanation.walkthrough: Change the second E of ELEVEN to O. An eleven is a team in football or cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: A hinged surface on a delta wing that works as both elevator and aileron, controlling the aircraft in flight.

clue.text: Home counties case for a sleeping pill

parts.note: the Home Counties surround London in the South East of England, abbreviated SE
the dative is a grammatical case, as in Latin or German

explanation.surface: A commuter from the suburbs around London carries a bag holding something to help them sleep.
explanation.walkthrough: The Home Counties are the counties around London, in England's South East (SE). 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A drug that calms or induces sleep, which a sleeping pill does.

clue.text: Holding on, in bar, after normal time?

definitions.text: Holding on, in bar, after normal time?

parts.words: Holding on, in bar, after normal time?
parts.note: reads like a drinker lingering in a pub past closing time, but in music a bar is a measure, and the direction asks for a note to be held for its full length or beyond

explanation.surface: A drinker lingers in the pub after closing time.
explanation.definitionFit: An Italian musical direction meaning held, telling the player to sustain a note for its full value.

clue.text: Pilot (mature), in cheapest accommodation on board?

parts.note: to pilot a vessel is to steer it
to mature is to age

explanation.surface: An older ship's pilot travels in the cheapest class.
explanation.definitionFit: On old passenger ships the lowest-fare section below decks, near the rudder gear, was where the cheapest tickets put you.
